## Profiles

A [profile](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/profiles) is a complete VS Code set-up: settings, keybindings, snippets, tasks, extensions and UI state. Each folder remembers which profile it was last opened with.

| Profile | Used for |
|---|---|
| `R` | All daily R work, on every machine. The one documented on [Settings](settings.qmd), [Keybindings](keybindings.qmd) and [Extensions](extensions.qmd). |
| `R-Lecturer` | Teaching. Kept close to what students get by default (light theme, default icons, Copilot mostly off), so what I show on the projector looks like their screen. See [below](#the-r-lecturer-profile). |
| Default | Folders that are not R projects, and the place for application-wide settings (see below). |

Other profiles (for Python and game development) are unrelated to R and not covered here.

### Profiles do not inherit

**A non-default profile's `settings.json` replaces the Default one; it is not layered on top.** Precedence is:

1. VS Code's built-in defaults,
2. the **active** profile's settings (Default *or* `R` *or* `R-Lecturer`, never a mix),
3. the workspace settings (`.vscode/settings.json` in the project).

So every profile must contain everything it needs. That is why the `R` profile repeats most of the Default settings.

The one exception is **application-scoped** settings, such as `update.mode` and `settingsSync.ignoredSettings`. They apply to the whole VS Code installation and are read **only from the Default profile**. VS Code greys them out in other profiles; that is expected.

### Where the files are

| What | Path |
|---|---|
| Default profile settings | `%APPDATA%\Code\User\settings.json` |
| Other profiles | `%APPDATA%\Code\User\profiles\<profile id>\settings.json` (also `keybindings.json`, `tasks.json`, `snippets\`) |
| Profile names, and which folder uses which profile | `%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\storage.json` (VS Code rewrites it on exit: do not edit it while VS Code runs) |

To move a folder to another profile, open it and pick the profile in the gear menu (bottom left). Delete obsolete profiles in the *Profiles* editor.

## Settings Sync

[Settings Sync](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/settings-sync) keeps profiles, settings, keybindings, snippets, tasks, extensions and UI state the same on every machine where you sign in. Change a setting once, on any machine, and it travels. That only works if **no machine-specific paths are in the synced files**, which is the main design rule of this set-up ([How the pieces fit](index.qmd#how-the-pieces-fit)).

### The gotcha: some settings never sync {#the-gotcha}

Sync silently skips three kinds of settings:

- those marked **machine** (they only make sense on one computer),
- those marked **machine-overridable**,
- those flagged **never to sync** by their extension.

vscode-R marks several of its settings like that: `r.consolePath`, `r.executablePath`, `r.consoleArgs`, `r.consoleSendDelay` and `r.plot.backend`. The symptom is confusing: *deleting* such a setting syncs, but a *new value* never arrives on the other machine.

The fix is the `settingsSync.ignoredSettings` list. A leading `-` means "include this after all":

```json
"settingsSync.ignoredSettings": ["-r.consolePath", "-r.plot.backend"]
```

- It must be in the **Default** profile (the download reads it from there) **and** in each synced profile (the upload reads it from the profile's own file).
- After changing the list, the receiving machine may need *Settings Sync: Sync Now* twice.
- To see what was actually uploaded: *Settings Sync: Show Synced Data*, or `%APPDATA%\Code\User\sync\<profile id>\settings\lastSyncsettings.json`.

The two settings it opts back in are safe to sync because they hold no paths: `r.consolePath` is just `"radian"` (found on `PATH`), and `r.plot.backend` is `"httpgd"`.

### What Settings Sync does not carry {#what-settings-sync-does-not-carry}

| Not synced | Where it lives | How I keep it in step |
|---|---|---|
| R, Rtools, Python, radian, Quarto, R packages | installed per machine | [Install, in order](install.qmd), the same versions everywhere |
| `PATH` and environment variables | Windows | the [PATH rules](outside_vscode.qmd#path-rules) |
| Task scripts | `%USERPROFILE%\.vscode-scripts\` | copied by hand ([Snippets and tasks](snippets_tasks.qmd)) |
| `.Rprofile` | `Documents\.Rprofile` | OneDrive shares the Documents folder ([Outside VS Code](outside_vscode.qmd#rprofile)) |
| PowerShell profiles | `Documents\PowerShell\` | OneDrive, as above |
| Which folder uses which profile | `storage.json` | set per machine (gear menu) |

## The Default profile

Every key of the Default profile, so nothing is hidden.

### Same as in the R profile

These 49 keys have exactly the same values as in the `R` profile and are explained on [Settings](settings.qmd): `[quarto]`, `claudeCode.hideOnboarding`, `diffEditor.ignoreTrimWhitespace`, `editor.accessibilitySupport`, `editor.defaultFormatter`, `editor.guides.bracketPairs`, `editor.inlineSuggest.enabled`, `editor.minimap.autohide`, `editor.minimap.maxColumn`, `editor.minimap.renderCharacters`, `editor.minimap.scale`, `editor.rulers`, `editor.stickyScroll.enabled`, `editor.tabSize`, `files.associations`, `git-graph.commitDetailsView.location`, `git-graph.date.type`, `git.autofetch`, `git.confirmSync`, `git.suggestSmartCommit`, `githubPullRequests.fileListLayout`, `githubPullRequests.pullBranch`, `hediet.vscode-drawio.resizeImages`, `markdown.extension.toc.updateOnSave`, `multiCommand.commands`, `quarto.mathjax.theme`, `quarto.render.previewReveal`, `r.alwaysUseActiveTerminal`, `r.bracketedPaste`, `r.consolePath`, `r.debugger.timeouts.startup`, `r.lsp.debug`, `r.lsp.diagnostics`, `r.plot.backend`, `r.plot.defaults.fullWindowMode`, `r.sessionWatcher`, `r.source.focus`, `resmongraphical.cpuusage.style`, `security.workspace.trust.untrustedFiles`, `settingsSync.ignoredSettings`, `terminal.integrated.cursorBlinking`, `terminal.integrated.cursorStyle`, `terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.windows`, `terminal.integrated.fontWeightBold`, `vsicons.dontShowNewVersionMessage`, `window.commandCenter`, `workbench.iconTheme`, `workbench.list.openMode`, `workbench.panel.defaultLocation`.

### Different from the R profile, or only here

| Setting | Value | What it does | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workbench.colorTheme` | `"Visual Studio 2019 Dark"` | Colour theme. | `R` uses `"Visual Studio Dark"`. |
| `editor.unicodeHighlight.nonBasicASCII` | `true` | Highlights non-ASCII characters. | `R` turns it off, because Czech names (`Ondřej`) would light up everywhere. |
| `[markdown]` | markdownlint as formatter | Formats Markdown with markdownlint. | `R` additionally shows whitespace changes in diffs of Markdown files. |
| `editor.formatOnPaste` | `true` | Formats pasted code. | Not set in `R`. |
| `terminal.integrated.env.windows` | `PATH` + `C:\Program Files\nodejs` | Adds Node.js to the terminal `PATH`. | A leftover: Node.js is on the system `PATH` already. |
| `remote.SSH.remotePlatform` | 4 hosts → `"linux"` | Tells Remote - SSH the OS of each server, so it does not ask. | Host names replaced with `server-N.example.org` here. |
| `update.mode` | `"start"` | Checks for VS Code updates only at start-up. | Application-scoped, so it belongs here. |
| `update.enableWindowsBackgroundUpdates` | `false` | Does not download and install updates in the background. | Updates happen when I restart, not mid-session. |
| `window.menuBarVisibility` | `"classic"` | Always shows the menu bar. | |
| `workbench.experimental.enableNewProfilesUI` | `true` | Was needed for the Profiles editor in older VS Code. | Leftover; the Profiles editor is standard now. |
| `grammarly.files.include` | Markdown, text, R, Quarto, R Markdown | Files Grammarly checks. | Grammarly is installed in the `R` profile; these settings only apply when using Default. |
| `grammarly.config.documentDialect` | `"british"` | British English. | |
| `grammarly.config.documentDomain` | `"academic"` | Academic writing style. | |
| `grammarly.config.suggestions.OxfordComma` | `true` | Suggests the Oxford comma. | |
| `grammarly.startTextCheckInPausedState` | `true` | Grammarly starts paused; turn it on when writing. | Keeps it quiet while coding. |
| `chatgpt.authenticationType` | `"Google Authentication"` | Sign-in method of an older ChatGPT extension. | Leftover. |
| `chatgpt.emailAddress` | `""` | Same extension. | Leftover, empty. |
| `chatgpt.localeOverride` | `"en-US"` | Same extension. | Leftover. |
| `codeium.enableConfig` | on for all, Markdown, Quarto | Languages for Codeium (an AI autocomplete). | Leftover: Codeium is not installed. |
| `aws.telemetry` | `false` | Turns off AWS Toolkit telemetry. | Leftover: AWS Toolkit is not installed. |
| `mssql.enableRichExperiences` | `true` | Newer UI of the SQL Server extension. | |

The leftovers are harmless (settings of extensions that are not installed do nothing).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
show_file("Default/settings.json", "json", label = "Default profile settings.json")
```

## The R-Lecturer profile

A copy of `R` that I trimmed towards VS Code's defaults, so that what I show in class matches what students see. The differences:

| Area | `R` | `R-Lecturer` | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Theme | Visual Studio Dark | Light Modern (the default) | Readable on projectors, and it is what students have. |
| Icons | vscode-icons | Material Icon Theme | |
| Terminal cursor | underline | line (the default) | |
| Copilot | on for most languages, no autocompletion as you type | off, except Quarto (slides) | Students do not have it; suggestions on the projector distract. |
| AI agent settings | Claude Code, Codex, chat auto-approve lists, ... | none | Not used in class. |
| Unicode highlighting | off | on (the default) | |
| Paste | | `editor.formatOnPaste: true` | |
| Quarto | `previewReveal: true` | preview in an external browser; visual editor wraps at 80 columns, spell-checks in en-GB | Slides are shown full-screen in the browser. |
| R | | `r.removeLeadingComments`, `r.session.levelOfObjectDetail: "Normal"`; still has the deprecated `r.plot.useHttpgd` | Cleaner code sent to the console in demos. |
| Formatters | YAML: Red Hat YAML; SCSS: built-in; SQL: SQL Server | YAML: Quarto; SCSS: SCSS Formatter; SQL: SQLTools | Different extension set. |
| File handling | panel on the right, empty-editor hint hidden, wrapped tabs, ... | VS Code defaults | Closer to the default layout. |
| Extensions | 72 | 65: no AI agents except Copilot Chat, no Docker, no CSV table editor; adds LaTeX, Zotero, LTeX, SQLTools, PostgreSQL, Excel/OOXML viewers | Matches the course content. See [Extensions](extensions.qmd) for the exact lists. |
| Keybindings | the [R set](keybindings.qmd) | its own set (see [Keybindings](keybindings.qmd)) | |
| Tasks | 2 | only *R: New scratch project* | |

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
show_file("R-Lecturer/settings.json", "json", label = "R-Lecturer settings.json")
show_file("R-Lecturer/tasks.json", "json", label = "R-Lecturer tasks.json")
```
